name: Nettspend
label: Grade A / Interscope
lede: Gunner Shepardson from Richmond, Virginia, recorded his breakout in about ten minutes in his mom's car, played Rolling Loud at sixteen, and put out his debut album on Interscope at eighteen.

eras.title: Skateboards and a country-singer dad
eras.text: A Richmond kid raised on Michael Jackson, Katy Perry and Justin Bieber, with a father who sang country. School ends in ninth grade, and by the end of 2022 he's taking music seriously.

years.h: Gunner Shepardson is born in Richmond, Virginia
years.p: One of four kids; his father is a country singer. Skateboarding, he tells Dazed, is where he learned to connect with people.
years.xp: To Dazed: "My dad missed my second birthday so he could go to a Willie Nelson concert." He says he was kicked out of his mother's house once and his father's three times. His first concert was Rainbow Kitten Surprise.

q: After all that Covid quarantine shit fucked my shit up
years.src: i-D · Rolling Stone: Xaviersobased, Nettspend, Yhapojj · Wikipedia: Nettspend · Interview: So Many Feelings: Meet Nettspend (2024)
years.h: Pushed by a friend, he starts posting songs to SoundCloud
years.p: He'd been rapping since fifth grade and had left school in ninth. His friend Nick Zuro gets him to commit, and the handle comes from thinking of "the internet."
years.xp:
i-D says he was kicked out of school in ninth grade after the COVID lockdown. He records vocals on BandLab, the phone app, wherever he is, per Rolling Stone.

Interview magazine dates the expulsion to 2022 and says it put him in touch with the local and online scene around NOVAGANG, 1c34, WitchGang and reklusl1ve. An early mixtape, Kickdoor, came before the 2023 singles.

eras.title: Ten minutes in his mom's car
eras.text: A year of SoundCloud songs, a friendship with Xaviersobased and a snippet that spreads on Twitter. By December, a New York club show gets out of hand.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Xaviersobased, Nettspend, Yhapojj · Wikipedia: Nettspend
years.h: Zuro introduces him to Xaviersobased; "shine n peace" catches on
years.p: The New York rapper and producer becomes his main ally. The Fader and the New York Times both list "shine n peace" among the year's best songs.
years.xp: Rolling Stone says Xavier was struck by his "demon-spawn stylings" among a field of imitation rage rappers, and passed his music on to Yhapojj. He was also briefly linked to the digicore collective Novagang. Another song, "what they say," got him a manager.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Xaviersobased, Nettspend, Yhapojj · Wikipedia: Drankdrankdrank
years.h: "drankdrankdrank," cut in his mother's car in the driveway
years.p: He records it in about ten minutes on BandLab over a Zoot beat. A snippet goes viral on Twitter before he self-releases it.

years.h: A Mercury Lounge show ends with the set moved to a van at a skate park
years.p: After a summer show at Market Hotel in Bushwick, the Mercury Lounge night ends with fans wrecking the venue's security equipment, per i-D.
years.xp: i-D says the trio then performed from a van at a nearby skate park.

eras.title: Sixteen, signed and divisive
eras.text: A song on the year's best lists, a festival debut, a sample that pulls his catalog off streaming, and a deal with Interscope and Grade A that ends in a debut mixtape with no guests.

years.p: The producer's track lands on best-song lists at the New York Times and Pitchfork.

years.cap: Nettspend at The Masquerade, Atlanta, December 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: Nettspend · Rolling Stone: Xaviersobased, Nettspend, Yhapojj · i-D
years.h: At sixteen, his first festival is Rolling Loud
years.p: Rolling Stone, that same week, describes him as ice-blond and still sixteen, a ninth-grade dropout recording wherever he stands.
years.xp: He told Rolling Stone the internet is scary as the hype builds, and that he posts and deletes a lot. He also played Restless Fest that year, per i-D.

years.p: The single with [[OsamaSon|35214d53-009b-45d9-8a00-6664325b9e2a]] is the first of their collaborations. He also has a cameo in Tommy Richman's "Devil Is a Lie" video that month.

years.h: "That One Song" samples Deftones, then disappears
years.p: The track flips [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]]' "Entombed." It's pulled from streaming, and most of his popular songs go with it.
years.xp: i-D, writing that September, says the removal and the sample-clearance situation were never explained.

years.src: Wikipedia: Early Life Crisis · Wikipedia: Nettspend · Interview: So Many Feelings: Meet Nettspend (2024)
years.h: Cole Bennett shoots "F*ck Swag" for Lyrical Lemonade
years.p: His first Lyrical Lemonade video. By year's end he is signed to Interscope and Grade A Productions.
years.xp: Around the same time he fronted a Heaven by Marc Jacobs campaign and turned up at Vogue World in Paris, per Interview magazine.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bad Ass F*cking Kid · Wikipedia: Nettspend · Pitchfork: BAD ASS F*CKING KID review (2024) · The Fader: Who's afraid of Nettspend? (2024) · Interview: So Many Feelings: Meet Nettspend (2024)
years.h: Bad Ass F*cking Kid: 15 tracks, 31 minutes, no features
years.p: The debut mixtape on Grade A and Interscope debuts at No. 197. Kenny Beats, Evilgiane and RokOnTheTrack are among the producers.
years.xp:
Reviews split: Pitchfork gave it 6.1, and critics singled out "Beach Leak." Meaghan Garvey's Pitchfork review called it "mostly derivative and incoherent" but granted him "a strange allure," and noted a Grimes sample on "Skipping Class." The Fader's headline went the other way: "He hasn't even peaked yet."

The tour started at Irving Plaza in New York, and in Los Angeles he brought out [[PinkPantheress|7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d]]. The Fader also reported that HBO was acquiring a documentary about him.

eras.title: Miu Miu, Vans and a debut album
eras.text: Fashion houses come calling, he turns eighteen, and the first studio album arrives with a browser game and a phone number. Reviews stay split.

years.cap: Nettspend on the Miu Miu runway, Paris Fashion Week, March 2025
years.h: Nettspend walks for Miu Miu at Paris Fashion Week
years.p: He shares the runway with Cortisa Star. Three days later the Vans-sponsored Invert tour starts, and on his 18th birthday he drops "Impact" with [[Xaviersobased|155cfd40-dcde-471e-acc0-32179916165c]].
years.xp: Dazed, interviewing him days before he turned 18, says he had recently bought a baby monkey named Elijah. Vans put him in a holiday ad that October.

years.h: Gone Too Soon is two songs long

years.src: Wikipedia: Early Life Crisis · Rolling Stone: Album Review · Wikipedia: Nettspend · The Fader: Nettspend doesn't fear failure on early life crisis (2026) · W Magazine: Nettspend Is Hard to Pin Down and Impossible to Ignore (2026)
years.p: Twenty-one tracks, a week late, with [[OsamaSon|35214d53-009b-45d9-8a00-6664325b9e2a]] on "Pain Talk" and YoungBoy Never Broke Again on "Masked Up." First week: 20,000 units.
years.xp:
He promoted it with an interactive browser game and a phone number, and walked in Demna's debut show for Gucci in Milan with Fakemink weeks earlier. The release slid from February 27 to March 6 with no reason given.

Pitchfork gave it 5.9. Rolling Stone's Jeff Ihaza liked it, saying it shows how rap might absorb new underground sounds. The Fader's Vivian Medithi heard OsamaSon's Psykotic and Che's Rest in Bass in it, and an artist whose "edges are starting to fray."

years.src: W Magazine: Nettspend Is Hard to Pin Down and Impossible to Ignore (2026)
years.h: The Early Life Crisis tour plays more than 30 cities
years.p: By September W magazine finds him 19, his blond-with-black-tips hair dyed magenta, and calling fame "a gift and a curse."
years.xp: "I feel like being famous was my only option," he told W. Of the new songs: "Some of it's vulnerable. Some of it's super turnt."

years.p: The compilation reaches streaming services on July 3. In between, at Summer Smash on June 13, he announces NXO, a joint album with [[OsamaSon|35214d53-009b-45d9-8a00-6664325b9e2a]].
